neighbours.label: verbs of attribution that link an effect to a cause or source (attributes, credits, cites, associates, bases ... on)
fire: Sales rose sharply this year, a jump the manager attributes to the new store layout.
The coach credits the team's recovery to a stricter training plan.
In her report, the author cites three earlier studies on soil erosion.
Many readers still associate the poet with rural landscapes.
The historian bases her argument on letters found in an attic.
Scientists attributed the fish deaths to a sudden drop in oxygen.
The mayor credited volunteers for cleaning up after the flood.
Critics often associate jazz with smoky clubs and late nights.
quiet: Sales rose sharply this year, a jump the manager announced at the meeting.
The coach describes the team's recovery as slow but steady.
In her report, the author summarizes three earlier studies on soil erosion.
Many readers still enjoy the poet's early work on rural landscapes.
The historian finished her argument after months in the archive.
Scientists counted the fish deaths along the river every morning.
The mayor thanked the crowd after the parade in the square.
Critics often write about jazz clubs and their late nights.
